why.matters: Security is the one defect a company cannot fix with an apology: a manager seeing another region's payroll is a reportable incident.
why.failure: A page filter or a hidden visual is used as "security"; anyone with Build permission or Analyze in Excel sees everything.
why.use: Whenever different people may see different rows of the same model.
why.avoid: When groups need entirely different models anyway, or when security must hold for direct SQL access too (secure the source as well).

steps: Manage roles → new role "West" with DAX filter on DimRegion: [RegionName] = "West". Create South, East, Central the same way.
View as → West. Note that the Region slicer now shows only West.
Publish, add a test user to the West role in the Service, open the report as them.
asg.exp: Cards show West totals only. The user cannot see other regions even by editing the report.

asg.t: Dynamic RLS with a mapping table
steps: Load UserRegionMapping. Relate UserRegionMapping[RegionKey] → DimRegion[RegionKey]? No: the mapping is many rows per user, so relate DimRegion (1) → UserRegionMapping (*) and set the relationship to bi-directional with "Apply security filter in both directions" on.

Handle the "All" row: change the DimRegion filter instead: VAR u = USERPRINCIPALNAME() RETURN CONTAINS(UserRegionMapping, UserRegionMapping[UserEmail], u, UserRegionMapping[RegionKey], DimRegion[RegionKey]) || CALCULATE(COUNTROWS(FILTER(UserRegionMapping, [UserEmail] = u && [AccessLevel] = "All"))) > 0
View as → Other user → nina.kowalski@northwind.example. Then grace.hollis@.
asg.exp: Nina sees West and East only. Grace sees all four. Dana sees West.

steps: Role "MyTeam": filter DimEmployee with PATHCONTAINS(DimEmployee[Path], LOOKUPVALUE(DimEmployee[EmployeeKey], DimEmployee[Email], USERPRINCIPALNAME())).
View as dana.whitfield@: she should see herself and everyone under her.
View as lily.chang@: she sees only herself.

asg.t: Test that RLS cannot be bypassed
steps: As the restricted user, try Analyze in Excel and try building a new report on the model (needs Build). Confirm RLS still applies.
Add a measure CALCULATE([Net Sales], ALL(DimRegion)) and confirm it still returns only the allowed regions.
Publish to a second workspace and note that role membership does not travel with it.
asg.exp: ALL does not remove RLS filters; role membership must be reassigned in each workspace.

int.q: Why can ALL() not bypass RLS?
int.a: RLS filters are applied at the storage layer before any DAX runs; they are not part of the filter context DAX manipulates.

Static: simple, one role per group, membership managed in the Service, breaks when groups change. Dynamic: one role, mapping table maintained by the business, needs USERPRINCIPALNAME and a bi-directional security filter, and the mapping must be refreshed.

int.q: What happens if a user is in two roles?
int.a: Filters are combined with OR: they see the union. Roles never intersect.

int.q: Does RLS apply to workspace Admins, Members and Contributors?
int.a: No. It applies only to users with Viewer role or with read permission via app/share. Anyone who can edit the model is exempt.

int.q: How does RLS interact with a bi-directional relationship?
int.a: Security filters only flow through a bi-directional relationship if "Apply security filter in both directions" is checked; otherwise the mapping-table role filters nothing on the fact side.
